name: Continuum: Consistency Tracker
subtitle: Daily habits, no streak resets
promotionalText: Continuum runs on one number now: the share of days you show up. Miss a day and it dips a point or two. It never goes back to zero.
description:
Miss a day. Nothing resets.

Continuum tracks each habit with one number: the share of days you actually showed up, over the last 66. It's free. There's nothing to sign up for and nothing to buy.

THE NUMBER
Streaks are brittle. One bad Tuesday and six weeks read 0, which is usually the day people quit. I built this app around streaks for a year, freezes included, and it was the wrong number to put in front of anyone who was mostly doing fine — the person who misses one Tuesday in six weeks is exactly the one a reset loses. Here a missed day costs a point or two. Show up tomorrow and it climbs back.

The count starts on your first day. A habit you began last week isn't scored against the weeks before it existed.

GETTING MORE CONSISTENT
Every number has an arrow beside it: how far it moved this week. The stats screen draws your last 12 weeks as bars, one per week, so you can see whether you're getting better — which matters more than whether you're perfect, because almost nobody is.

NEVER MISS TWICE
Missing once is normal. Missing twice is how habits end. Skip a day and you get one quiet nudge the next evening at 8pm; mark it and the card says you're back on it.

66 DAYS, NOT IN A ROW
Lally et al. (2009) found habits take a median of 66 days of practice to become automatic, and that one missed day didn't set people back. So a habit here is formed at 66 days done. Any order.

THE GRID
Every habit gets a 66-day grid, one square per day. Your number is exactly the filled squares over the squares so far.

MARKING DONE
Press and hold. Haptics build under your thumb and release when the day registers (hard to do by accident). Forgot yesterday? Tap once, then hold.

WIDGETS
Home screen and lock screen, percentage included. Mark a habit done without opening the app.

THE REST
A year heatmap per habit. Share cards. iCloud sync across your devices. Dark, monospaced, deliberately plain.

There's no social feed, and no streak to lose.
